proof:
# An additive upper-tail reserve in every dimension d>=2

This is an actual convex-body theorem. It extends the planar boundary-gain
argument without assuming monotonicity of local mixed volumes. Its proof
uses finitely many actual translations when B is a polytope, followed by
an explicit volume-convergence argument for general B.

## 1. The theorem

Let d>=2 and write R^d=R^(d-1) times R, with coordinates (x,t). Let
A and B be full-dimensional compact convex bodies. Assume

    t(A)=[l,h],       t(B) subset [-c,1],
    l<-1,            h>c>0.

Let S be any actual segment joining a point of A at level l to a point
of A at level h. Then

    |(A+B) intersect {t>=0}| - |(S+B) intersect {t>=0}|
        >= |A intersect {t>=c}|.                         (1)

All volumes are ordinary d-dimensional Lebesgue volume with the usual
normalization. All halfspaces are closed. No selected center or body
outside the given sets is used in (1).

In fact the proof gives a stronger statement: after making S vertical
by a determinant-one shear preserving t, it is enough that S subset A,
that S has constant transverse coordinate, and that min_B t>=-c.
No upper bound on t(B), extremality of the endpoints, or inequalities
l<-1 and h>c are needed for this stronger version. The stated original
hypotheses guarantee these requirements and a nonempty upper tail.

The assertion is false in d=1. For example A=S=[-2,3], B=[-1,0],
c=1 gives identical sums on the left of (1), hence zero difference,
while |A intersect {t>=1}|=2. The positive transverse dimension is
essential to the proof and to the assertion.

## 2. Coordinates and the elementary finite translation lemma

Write the endpoints of S as (x_-,l),(x_+,h). The linear shear

    (x,t) -> (x-[(x_+-x_-)/(h-l)]t,t)

has determinant one, preserves every t halfspace, and makes S have
a constant transverse coordinate x_0. It commutes with Minkowski
addition because it is linear. We work in these coordinates and
retain x_0 explicitly, so no affine-translation identity is hidden.

First suppose B is a full-dimensional polytope. Its transverse
projection P is a full-dimensional polytope in R^m, m=d-1>=1.
List its distinct vertices p_1,...,p_N. For each choose an actual
point b_i=(p_i,t_i) in B. Such a point exists by the definition of
projection, and t_i>=-c. No condition on uniqueness or the dimension
of the vertical fiber over p_i is required.

Define the open normal regions

    Omega_i={v in R^m: v.p_i>v.p_j for every j!=i}.

The complement of their union is contained in the finite union of
hyperplanes {v:v.(p_i-p_j)=0}, i!=j, and therefore has m-dimensional
measure zero. For v in Omega_i, p_i uniquely maximizes v.p over
the WHOLE projected polytope P. Also v!=0.

Here are the two exact properties used below.

1. For v in Omega_i,

       v.(v+p_i)=|v|^2+h_P(v)>h_P(v),

   so v+p_i is outside P.

2. The translated transverse regions Omega_i+p_i are pairwise
   disjoint. Indeed, suppose v in Omega_i, w in Omega_j, i!=j,
   and v+p_i=w+p_j. The two strict maximizing inequalities give

       (v-w).(p_i-p_j)>0.

   But the alleged equality gives v-w=p_j-p_i, making this
   inner product -|p_i-p_j|^2<0, a contradiction.

These facts are finite linear geometry. They require neither
differentiability of a support function nor an unproved transport map.

## 3. A disjoint actual translation of the upper tail

Put E=A intersect {t>=c}. Partition it into the Borel pieces

    E_i={(x,t) in E: x-x_0 in Omega_i}.

The pieces cover E up to a d-dimensional null set: the omitted set
lies in finitely many transverse hyperplanes times a bounded t interval.
This follows directly from Fubini; m>=1 and A is bounded.

Translate each E_i by the corresponding ACTUAL point b_i in B.
Every image point belongs to A+B. Its height is at least c+t_i>=0,
so it belongs to the tested closed halfspace. Its transverse coordinate
has the form x_0+v+p_i with v in Omega_i and is outside x_0+P by
property 1. Since the transverse projection of S+B is exactly x_0+P,
this image point is outside S+B.

The translated pieces E_i+b_i are pairwise disjoint, because their
transverse projections lie in the disjoint regions from property 2.
Translations preserve d-volume, hence

    |union_i(E_i+b_i)|=sum_i|E_i|=|E|.

Finally S subset A implies S+B subset A+B. Consequently the difference
of the two captured volumes in (1) equals the volume of their set
difference, and that set difference contains the displayed disjoint
union. This proves (1) for polytope B. The argument works with the
actual body A throughout; no approximation or polyhedrality of A is
needed.

## 4. Passage to an arbitrary convex body B

Choose an increasing sequence of full-dimensional inscribed polytopes
B_j subset B converging to B in Hausdorff distance. One construction
is to take convex hulls of successively more points of a countable
dense subset of B, including a fixed affine-independent set at the
first stage. Compactness ensures the Hausdorff distances epsilon_j
tend to zero. Each B_j still satisfies min t>=-c, so the proved
polytope inequality uses the SAME fixed upper tail E.

Here is a complete uniform volume-convergence justification. Choose
z and rho>0 with z+rho B_d subset B_1. Put

    lambda_j=epsilon_j/(rho+epsilon_j).

The support-function inequalities h_B<=h_Bj+epsilon_j|u| and
h_Bj>=u.z+rho|u| imply

    (1-lambda_j)B+lambda_j z subset B_j.             (2)

Indeed the support of the left side is at most h_Bj plus
[(1-lambda_j)epsilon_j-lambda_j rho]|u|=0. Support inequalities
characterize inclusion of compact convex sets by separation.

Fix a_0 in A and s_0 in S. By convexity and (2),

    (1-lambda_j)(A+B)+lambda_j(a_0+z) subset A+B_j,
    (1-lambda_j)(S+B)+lambda_j(s_0+z) subset S+B_j.

Both sums have full dimension because B is full dimensional. Since
the approximating sums are contained in the limiting sums, their
total missing volumes are bounded by

    [1-(1-lambda_j)^d]|A+B|,
    [1-(1-lambda_j)^d]|S+B|,

respectively, and tend to zero. For ANY fixed measurable halfspace H,
the missing captured volumes are at most these total missing volumes.
Thus both captured volumes in (1) converge, with no assumption about
boundary mass and no interchange of optimizing normals or centers.
Passing to the limit in the fixed inequality proves (1) for B.

## 5. Sharpness of the coefficient and the mixed-fiber consequence

The coefficient one in front of the upper-tail volume is best possible.
Let m=d-1>=1, fix l<-1 and h>c>0, and take

    A=[-1,1]^m times [l,h],
    S={0} times [l,h],
    B_epsilon=[-epsilon,epsilon]^m times [-c,-c+epsilon],

with epsilon>0 small. These are actual full-dimensional convex bodies
and t(B_epsilon) subset [-c,1]. The left side of (1) is exactly

    [(2+2epsilon)^m-(2epsilon)^m](h-c+epsilon),

whereas |A intersect {t>=c}|=2^m(h-c). Their ratio tends to one
as epsilon decreases to zero. Thus no larger universal coefficient
works, even for boxes and the central extreme segment. This is a
sharp infimum statement, not a claim of equality for positive epsilon.

For actual mixed fibers with (A+B)/2 subset K and
q=|K intersect {t>=0}|, the proved reserve gives

    2^d q >= |(S+B) intersect {t>=0}|
                    + |A intersect {t>=c}|.          (3)

The factor 2^d is exactly the ambient continuous midpoint Jacobian.
In the canonical d-simplex endpoint setting, its t range is [-d,1],
so c=d and the reserve is the actual far tail above level d.
This supplies a valid all-dimensional extension of the planar additive
reserve. It does not by itself establish an all-dimensional sharp roof
capacity or the original mixed-integer depth conjecture.
